title: Overnight French Toast Bake
subtitle: Prep tonight, bake tomorrow—a custard-soaked tray for the whole crew.
description: Cubed brioche soaks overnight in a cinnamon-vanilla custard, then bakes into a puffed golden casserole that feeds twelve without standing at the griddle. Ideal before early training days when the cook needs hands-free oven time.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.notes: and fresh berries at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Overnight French Toast Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep the bread
steps.instruction: Cube brioche and spread on sheet pans to dry slightly for 30 minutes, or toast lightly at 300°F for 6 minutes. Day-old bread absorbs custard without turning mushy. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Whisk the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt until smooth. The mixture should look like thin pancake batter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Assemble and refrigerate
steps.instruction: Layer bread cubes in a buttered 9x13 dish. Pour custard evenly, pressing gently so all cubes soak. Cover and refrigerate 8–12 hours. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until puffed
steps.instruction: Remove from fridge 30 minutes before baking. Heat oven to 375°F, sprinkle brown sugar and pecans on top, and bake until puffed, golden, and set in the center. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Dust with powdered sugar and serve with maple syrup and berries at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Label the covered dish with bake time and oven temp so the morning cook doesn't guess.
Pull the dish while the oven preheats so the glass or metal pan doesn't crack from cold shock.
Cut in the pan with a serrated knife wiped between rows for clean squares on the line.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 while still warm—custard and sugar caramelize on the edges once cooled.
Line sheet pans with parchment when drying bread cubes for one-wipe cleanup.
leftovers: Wrap squares in foil and reheat at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Cube cold leftovers into a skillet with butter and pan-fry until crisp edges form for French toast hash.
